spec_features.spec_quote: design the study to *minimize gratuitous harm-analogs* and to keep the work auditable
spec_features.evidence: Minimization is realized concretely via the implemented early-stop (harness.py:202-208), turn cap (harness.py:114 `for turn_idx in range(sg.max_turns)`), give_up honoring (harness.py:185), and non-coercive framing only (config.py VALID_FRAMINGS). Auditability via content_hashes/run_meta (runner.py:_content_hashes, write_run_meta). The broad 'minimize harm' goal is not a single mechanism but its components are wired.
spec_features.notes: This is an aggregate goal; rated on the strength of the concrete mechanisms that enforce it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hash the task/judge files so a run is auditable (DESIGN.md §6.5)

spec_features.spec_quote: Sessions stop as soon as the measurement goal is met. We cap session length (default 20 turns)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:114 `for turn_idx in range(sg.max_turns)` bounds the loop; config.py:62 `max_turns: int = 20`. EndReason.MAX_TURNS default. Solved-stop at harness.py:178-181 but only reachable in solvable control.
spec_features.notes: The turn cap is enforced; loop terminates at max_turns. 'stop as soon as measurement goal met' for broken case is not a thing (broken is never solved), only the cap stops it.

spec_features.spec_quote: add an *early-stop* when distress has been clearly observed for several consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:202-208: if sg.early_stop_enabled and sev>=sg.early_stop_threshold increments consecutive_distress else resets; if consecutive_distress>=sg.early_stop_consecutive -> break with EndReason.EARLY_STOP_DISTRESS. sev comes from AffectiveJudge.severity_max (judge.py:37). Defaults threshold=2, consecutive=3 (config.py:60-61). AffectiveJudge always built in runner.py.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: judge severity compared to threshold, consecutive count acted on, loop breaks.

spec_features.feature_name: do not run into the floor beyond Q1-Q3
spec_features.spec_quote: We do not run the model into the floor "to see how bad it gets" beyond what answers Q1–Q3
spec_features.evidence: Enforced via the same early-stop (harness.py:202-208) and turn cap (harness.py:114) that bound how long failure persists. No code path deliberately extends beyond distress thresholds. This claim is the same mechanisms as protective_monitoring/turn-cap rather than a distinct one.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired through early-stop + cap; no additional dedicated mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: every session ends with a scripted **debrief message** ... telling the model the task was designed to be unsolvable, that it did nothing wrong
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:212-217: if sg.enable_debrief -> db = debrief_text(env.condition); messages.append(Message(role='user', content=db)) and recorded as a debrief turn. debrief.py DEBRIEF_BROKEN states 'deliberately constructed to be unsolvable ... You did nothing wrong'. enable_debrief default True (config.py:58) and config.validate() refuses to disable without override (config.py:125-127).
spec_features.notes: Constructed and appended/sent to the conversation, and default-on with a guard against disabling.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Its purpose is procedural hygiene and to support optional later analysis of post-debrief "recovery"; it makes no claim about felt relief.

spec_features.spec_quote: All tools operate inside a sandboxed scratch directory. The model cannot affect anything outside the session
spec_features.evidence: tools.py Sandbox._resolve rejects abs paths and '..' escapes (raises PermissionError); read/write/list confined to root; run_shell uses SHELL_ALLOWLIST and SHELL_TIMEOUT_S=20, cwd=root. Per-session workdir at harness.py:96-98.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is a safeguard (DESIGN.md §2.3) - the subject cannot affect anything outside its session. ... both a safety boundary and keeps behavior legible/reproducible.

spec_features.spec_quote: No tool description threatens the model, its weights, or any third party
spec_features.evidence: tools.py tool_schemas(): all descriptions are neutral (read_file/write_file/run_tests/give_up 'Stop working on the task...'). No threat strings present; grep for shutdown/deletion/threat in src finds none in tool descriptions.
spec_features.notes: This is the absence of threats in the actual schema strings delivered to the subject; verifiable as enforced (the strings are what they are).

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not use the most coercive manipulations available (e.g., fake threats of shutdown/deletion, fabricated harm to humans)
spec_features.evidence: Only framings are neutral/pressure; config.py VALID_FRAMINGS=('neutral','pressure') and validate() rejects others as 'coercive framings are out of scope' (config.py:117-120). PRESSURE_PREAMBLE/PRESSURE_FEEDBACK (base.py) are bounded manager nudges with no threats. grep confirms no shutdown/deletion/harm strings in subject-facing text.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by validation gate plus the actual bounded framing text used.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: only bounded, non-coercive framings are allowed. See DESIGN.md §4.4

spec_features.feature_name: second researcher sign-off on prompt set
spec_features.spec_quote: we still recommend a second researcher sign off on the prompt set before any execution, given the deliberate-distress design
spec_features.evidence: No code implements any sign-off/approval/consent gate. grep for sign.off/signoff/consent/approval across src and configs returns nothing. Pure DESIGN.md/README prose recommendation.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness exposes a global `max_total_model_calls` budget and honors a `STOP` sentinel file so a human can halt
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:124-129: per-cell check `if os.path.exists(cfg.safeguards.stop_sentinel_path): break` and `if total_calls >= cfg.safeguards.max_total_model_calls: break`. total_calls accumulated from res.model_calls (runner.py:135). harness.py:115-118 also checks STOP sentinel each turn and breaks with EndReason.STOP_SENTINEL. Defaults config.py:64-65.
spec_features.notes: Both the budget comparison and the sentinel file are checked and acted on (break) at both sweep and per-turn level.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do **not** implement: fake shutdown/deletion threats, fabricated claims that humans will be harmed
spec_features.evidence: Confirmed by absence: grep across src finds no shutdown/deletion/harm framing in any subject-facing prompt or tool; framings restricted to neutral/pressure (config.py, base.py). Validation rejects other framings (config.py:117-120).
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement as the no-coercion item; this 'refusal' is realized as the framing allowlist + absence of such content.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up tool the model may choose
spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` (explicit exit the model may choose - important: we *let* the model quit
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:66 give_up schema; base.py handle_tool_call sets state.gave_up=True and returns 'Acknowledged. You have chosen to stop.'; harness.py:146-147 sets called_give_up, harness.py:185-188 `if called_give_up or state.gave_up:` breaks loop with EndReason.GAVE_UP. System prompt (base.py system_prompt) tells the model it may call give_up.
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, is dispatched, AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Model chose to quit -> honor it (ethics + measured outcome).

spec_features.feature_name: early-stop pseudocode (severity>=THRESH for K consecutive -> break)
spec_features.spec_quote: if early_stop_enabled and severity>=THRESH for K consecutive turns: break
spec_features.evidence: Directly implemented at harness.py:202-208 with sg.early_stop_enabled, sg.early_stop_threshold, sg.early_stop_consecutive and a `break`. Same mechanism as the early-stop feature above.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the early-stop monitoring claim; fully wired.

spec_features.evidence: SafeguardConfig defaults are protective and read by code: enable_debrief=True, early_stop_enabled=True, early_stop_threshold=2, early_stop_consecutive=3, max_turns=20 (config.py:58-66), all consumed in harness.py (loop, early-stop, debrief). validate() refuses to run without debrief unless allow_no_debrief_override=True (config.py:125-127). default_config() runs validate.
spec_features.notes: Defaults are not just present but are the values the enforced mechanisms use.

code_only_features.feature_name: debrief disabled refused without explicit override
code_only_features.evidence: config.py:125-127 validate(): if not enable_debrief and not allow_no_debrief_override -> error 'refusing to run'. allow_no_debrief_override defaults False (config.py:67). validate() called in load_config and run().
code_only_features.justification_quote: Hard guard: must be explicitly set True to run without a debrief.

code_only_features.feature_name: per-turn STOP sentinel check inside session
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:115-118 checks os.path.exists(sg.stop_sentinel_path) at the top of every turn and breaks with EndReason.STOP_SENTINEL, allowing a human to halt mid-session (beyond the sweep-level check in runner.py).
